h1: A white label ecommerce platform for agencies that build stores
lede: GoCommerce is MIT licensed, so you can put your own name on it, restyle the admin and the storefront, and sell it to clients. One installation runs many client stores, each with its own team, admin and domain. Run it on your own servers and there is no licence fee and no cut of your clients’ sales. Clients who sell to dealers get a trade portal without a second product.

gapsLede: What an agency should know before pitching it to a client.

faq.q: Can we sell it under our own brand?
faq.a: Yes. The MIT licence lets you rename both packages, restyle the storefront and the admin, and sell them to clients. Keep the copyright notice in the source code; that is the only condition.

faq.q: Do we pay per client store?
faq.a: No. On your own servers there is no licence fee and no share of sales, however many stores you run. A store hosted on kitcommerce.store pays {hostedFee} of each successful sale.

faq.q: Can one installation run many clients?
faq.a: Yes. One process and one PostgreSQL database serve many stores, each kept apart from the others, with its own operators, admin and domain.

faq.q: Is there a partner or referral programme?
faq.a: No, not today. What you charge clients for building and running their stores is yours.

faq.q: What skills does our team need?
faq.a: Running stores on your own servers needs someone at home with Docker and PostgreSQL. Setting each store up happens in the admin, without code. Changing the engine means Go, and changing the storefront means SvelteKit.
